metadata.description: The country whose criminal procedure and legal system are the subject of the analysis.
The single national authority responsible for instituting criminal proceedings on behalf of the State in South Africa.
The national police force responsible for investigating crimes and carrying out arrests.
The highest court in South Africa for all constitutional matters, including the validity of criminal procedures.
The second-highest court in South Africa, which hears appeals from the High Courts.
Superior courts with original jurisdiction over serious crimes and appellate jurisdiction over lower courts.
Lower courts that handle the majority of criminal cases and conduct preliminary inquiries for children.
Former President of South Africa, whose legal cases significantly impacted the interpretation of prosecutorial independence.
Politician involved in a high-profile fraud case that tested the limits of plea and sentence agreements.
Appellant in the landmark case Sanderson v Attorney-General, which established the criteria for a 'reasonable time' for trial.
An investigator whose case against the NPA clarified the requirements for obtaining a 'nolle prosequi' certificate.
A former elite investigative unit involved in high-profile criminal investigations.
The body responsible for providing legal representation to indigent accused persons to prevent 'substantial injustice'.
A specialized police unit responsible for investigating crimes involving children.
The landmark 1995 Constitutional Court case that abolished the death penalty in South Africa.
A key legal event concerning the exercise of prosecutorial discretion and political interference.
A critical case that ended docket privilege and established the right of access to witness statements.
A notable inquest into the deaths of the 'Cradock Four', illustrating the use of specialized judicial inquiries.

edges.description: The NPA is the primary state body for prosecutions in South Africa.
The national police force of South Africa.
The Constitutional Court heard and decided the case that abolished the death penalty.
The SCA ruled on matters regarding the NPA's decisions concerning Jacob Zuma.
Jacob Zuma's prosecutions involved significant legal disputes with the NPA.
Yengeni challenged the validity of a plea and sentence agreement with the NPA.
Sanderson challenged the NPA's delay in bringing his case to trial.
The CPU investigated the allegations against Sanderson.
Singh was a member of the Directorate of Special Operations (Scorpions).
Singh sought a 'nolle prosequi' certificate from the NPA to pursue a private prosecution.
The High Court (and later Constitutional Court) decided on docket access in the Shabalala case.
The Legal Aid Board provides defense services in the lower courts.
